title: Local chain representatives from a perfect constant complex
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with final object $X$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $F^\bullet$ be a bounded cochain complex of $R$-modules, meaning that $F^q=0$ outside a finite interval, whose terms are finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Let $\mathcal G^\bullet$ be any cochain complex of sheaves of $\underline R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\underline R$ and $\underline F^\bullet$ the constant ring sheaf and the termwise constant complex [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $Q$ for localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every morphism $\psi:Q(\underline F^\bullet)\to Q(\mathcal G^\bullet)$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to X\}$ and chain maps $a_i:\underline F^\bullet|_{U_i}\to\mathcal G^\bullet|_{U_i}$ with $Q(a_i)=\psi|_{U_i}$. The restrictions are to the localized ringed sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No boundedness is assumed for $\mathcal G^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 09BD, lemma-map-out-of-locally-constant; equivalently the constant finite-projective-source specialization of Tag 08FR(1), lemma-local-actual.

proof.text: Put $E^\bullet=\underline F^\bullet$ and choose integers $a\leq b$ outside which its terms vanish. For each q choose generators of $F^q$, giving a surjection $p_q:R^{n_q}\to F^q$. Projectivity lifts $\mathrm{id}_{F^q}$ through $p_q$, so there is $j_q:F^q\to R^{n_q}$ with $p_qj_q=\mathrm{id}$. Apply the constant module functor. Sheafification preserves finite products, so the coordinate maps identify $\underline{R^{n_q}}$ with $\underline R^{n_q}$; these are $\underline R$-linear because both scalar actions extend the same constant presheaf action. Thus there are $\underline R$-linear maps $J_q:E^q\to\underline R^{n_q}$ and $P_q:\underline R^{n_q}\to E^q$ with $P_qJ_q=\mathrm{id}$. Also $\underline0=0$. This proves that E is bounded with finite-free retract terms, i.e. strictly perfect as in Stacks 08FL.

source.place: Tag 09BD (lemma-map-out-of-locally-constant); Tag 08FL (definition-strictly-perfect); the finite-projective retract calculation

proof.text: Apply the right-fraction representation in the homotopy category of the abelian category of $\underline R$-modules; its quasi-isomorphisms admit the required right calculus. Choose a complex $B^\bullet$, a quasi-isomorphism $s:B^\bullet\to E^\bullet$ and a chain map $f:B^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ representing the homotopy-class arrows, with $\psi=Q(f)\circ Q(s)^{-1}$. The cone $C^\bullet=C(s)^\bullet$ is acyclic. Use the cone convention $C^n=E^n\oplus B^{n+1}$ and $d_C^n(x,y)=(d_E^n x+s^{n+1}y,-d_B^{n+1}y)$, and let $i:E^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ be $i^n(x)=(x,0)$.

source.place: Tag 08FR (lemma-local-actual), fraction presentation; Tag 08FQ (lemma-lift-through-quasi-isomorphism), cone obstruction; Derived Categories 05RT (lemma-acyclic)

proof.text: All subsequent constructions may be restricted to a slice $\mathcal C/V$. This site is small: its objects and arrows are subsets of sets of arrows and composable pairs in $\mathcal C$. The site-module sheafification theorem, applied with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$, supplies abelian sheafification on this slice, as required by the forgetful-functor lemma. Its module restriction functor is additive sectionwise and exact: kernels are sectionwise; epimorphisms are preserved since the faithful exact forgetful functor to abelian sheaves and the general-site epimorphism criterion express them by local lifts, and a covering of an object over V is precisely a covering of its underlying object. Faithfulness reflects vanishing cokernels, so these assertions also give exactness in the module category. Therefore restriction preserves the acyclicity of C and the quasi-isomorphism s, and the exact-functor localization comparison defines $\psi|_V=Q(f|_V)\circ Q(s|_V)^{-1}$. Finite-free retract maps remain retract maps upon restriction; finite products are sectionwise. Restriction along $X$ itself identifies $\mathcal C/X$ with $\mathcal C$, since X is final.

source.place: Tags 08FP (lemma-local-homotopy) and 08FQ (lemma-lift-through-quasi-isomorphism), restriction to localized ringed sites; Modules on Sites 03DA (lemma-abelian)

proof.text: Here is the local lifting calculation used at each degree, written for any object V. If $p:M\to N$ is an epimorphism of modules on $\mathcal C/V$ and $r:E^q|_V\to N$ is a module morphism, consider $rP_q:\mathcal O_V^{n_q}\to N$, where $\mathcal O=\underline R$. Evaluate on the finitely many standard basis sections at $V/V$. The underlying abelian map of p is epic, so the general-site local-surjectivity criterion gives local preimages of each of these sections. Take a common refinement of those finitely many coverings. On each member W the chosen preimages define an $\mathcal O_W$-linear map $L:\mathcal O_W^{n_q}\to M|_W$ by sending the standard basis to these preimages: on an object $T\to W$ it sends $(c_j)_j\in\mathcal O(T)^{n_q}$ to $\sum_j c_j(m_j|_T)$. For $T'\to T$, semilinearity of restriction gives $\left(\sum_j c_j(m_j|_T)\right)|_{T'}=\sum_j(c_j|_{T'})(m_j|_{T'})$, so these maps form a sheaf morphism. Its composite with p equals $rP_q|_W$, hence $LJ_q|_W$ lifts $r|_W$. If $n_q=0$, take the zero lift and the identity covering. This is the basis-and-retract proof of Stacks 08FN, rather than an additional lemma assumed without citation.

source.place: Tag 08FN (lemma-local-lift-map), proof by lifting finitely many basis sections; Sites 00W6 (lemma-common-refinement)

proof.text: Construct a null homotopy of i by finite descending induction, successively refining the covering. Start with $h^q=0$ for $q>b$. Suppose $h^{n+1},h^{n+2},\ldots$ have been constructed on the current member and $i^q=d_C^{q-1}h^q+h^{q+1}d_E^q$ holds for $q>n$. Put $r^n=i^n-h^{n+1}d_E^n$. Since i is a chain map, $d_C^nr^n=i^{n+1}d_E^n-(i^{n+1}-h^{n+2}d_E^{n+1})d_E^n=0$. Thus $r^n$ factors through $Z^n(C)=\ker d_C^n$. Acyclicity says that $d_C^{n-1}:C^{n-1}\to Z^n(C)$ is epic. Apply the basis-and-retract calculation of Step 4 to lift $r^n$ locally to $h^n:E^n\to C^{n-1}$. This gives the equation at degree n, while previous equations survive restriction. Continue for $n=b,b-1,\ldots,a$. Transitivity of coverings makes the finite successive refinements a covering $\{U_i\to X\}$. Set $h^q=0$ for $q<a$; the remaining equations are identities between maps from zero terms. This supplies a homotopy $i|_{U_i}=d_Ch+hd_E$ on each member. No infinite intersection of coverings and no boundedness of B or $\mathcal G$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 08FP (lemma-local-homotopy), finite induction with the degreewise homotopy equations expanded; Tag 08FN (lemma-local-lift-map)

proof.text: On each $U_i$ write the two components of $h^n:E^n\to C^{n-1}=E^{n-1}\oplus B^n$ as $(u^n,t^n)$. The first component of $i=d_Ch+hd_E$ is $\mathrm{id}_{E^n}=d_E^{n-1}u^n+s^nt^n+u^{n+1}d_E^n$; its second component is $0=-d_B^nt^n+t^{n+1}d_E^n$. Consequently t is a chain map $E|_{U_i}\to B|_{U_i}$ and $s|_{U_i}\circ t$ is homotopic to $\mathrm{id}_{E|_{U_i}}$. Localization factors through the homotopy category, so $Q(s|_{U_i})Q(t)=\mathrm{id}$; as $Q(s|_{U_i})$ is invertible, $Q(t)=Q(s|_{U_i})^{-1}$. Define $a_i=f|_{U_i}\circ t$. Then $Q(a_i)=Q(f|_{U_i})Q(s|_{U_i})^{-1}=\psi|_{U_i}$ by Step 3, which proves every clause of the item. If E is zero, all these maps and equations are zero and the identity covering suffices.
